Menubar.modal.semantic: whether the menubar is modal (children menus inherit the modal behaviour).

Menubar.disabled.semantic: disables the whole menubar (cascades to the menus inside).

Menubar.orientation.semantic: menu bar orientation; drives which arrow keys move between top-level menus (vertical menubars behave like the docs' example where submenu Positioners use side 'inline-end').

Menubar.loopFocus.semantic: arrow-key focus wraps to the first item when the end of the bar is reached.

className / style / render.type: string | ((state: Menubar.State) => ...) / CSSProperties | fn / ReactElement | fn

dataAttributes: data-has-submenu-open — present when any submenu within the menubar is open
data-modal — present when the menubar is modal
renderProp: Menubar accepts the standard `render` prop (ReactElement | (props: HTMLProps, state: Menubar.State) => ReactElement) plus state-driven className/style; it renders a <div> by default. Custom components: useRender; merging: mergeProps/mergePropsN.
controlled: None — Menubar owns no open/value state. Every child `<Menu.Root>` keeps its own `open`/`defaultOpen`/`onOpenChange` (and its own disabled prop); the menubar only coordinates focus. There is no value/onValueChange on Menubar.
keyboard: Roving focus across the top-level `<Menu.Trigger>` elements: horizontal menubars use ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, vertical menubars use ArrowUp/ArrowDown; `loopFocus` (default true) wraps at the ends. Each contained Menu.Root supplies the rest of the behaviour (ArrowUp/Down inside the popup, Home/End, typeahead via item `label`, Escape to dismiss, submenu arrow keys). Disabled menus inside the bar are skipped by focus.
notableDifferences: Menubar is a single component with no sub-parts; you nest ordinary `<Menu.Root>` children (each with its own Trigger/Portal/Positioner/Popup). React Aria builds a menubar from a Toolbar-like composite of MenuTriggers with `useMenuTrigger` — there is no per-menubar MenuTrigger part here.
Menubar is modal by default (`modal=true`), which is unusual for a menu bar and affects scroll locking/outside pointer behaviour.
State vocabulary is container-level only: data-orientation, data-modal, data-has-submenu-open. There is no data-disabled on the menubar itself even though `disabled` exists.
No value/selection state and no imperative handle — open state stays with the individual menus (a disabled `<Menu.Root disabled>` shows in the docs example).
